lessons.title: Daily Bite
lessons.objective: One card a day to stay sharp.

payload.prompt: When the caution drops with 50 laps left, what opens?

options.text: A pit cycle where teams pit in a similar window.
The fuel window, so everyone must pit.
A restart lane, where drivers pick inside or outside.

explanation.correct: Right. A caution opens the pit cycle; teams converge on pit road in a rhythm based on fuel and tires.
explanation.incorrect: A caution opens a pit cycle. Teams pit in a similar window because fuel and tires run out around the same laps. That synchronization is the cycle.

options: so it sounds like a stadium
gaps.correct: so it sounds like a stadium

explanation.correct: Perfect. Bristol's banking is famously steep, which lets cars go fast and creates multi-groove racing you can hear from the stands.
explanation.incorrect: Bristol Motor Speedway has steep banking that makes the cars go fast and creates an iconic stadium sound. It is one of the most dramatic tracks.

payload.prompt: Does the car behind always have an easier time in dirty air?

scene.alt: Two cars in traffic, one ahead and one behind, at a fast track.

choices.label: No, dirty air makes it harder to pass.
Yes, dirty air is free speed.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Dirty air is turbulent and kills grip, making the trailing car slower and unable to pass.
explanation.incorrect: Dirty air is the chaotic wake behind a car. It reduces front grip and makes passing harder, not easier. The leader has the advantage.

payload.prompt: Match each term to the 2026 Chase structure.

pairs.definition: The drivers who make the Chase after the 26-race regular season.
Darlington through Homestead; no eliminations, just one long race for points.
Homestead-Miami, race 36, where the most points wins the title.
Seeds 1-16 start at 2,100, 2,075, 2,065, 2,060 then -5 per seed to 2,000.

distractorDefinitions: The driver with the most wins always makes the Chase.
Eliminations cut the field after every four races.

explanation.summary: The 2026 Chase is 16 drivers, ten races, no eliminations, and a points reset that gives the regular-season champion a cushion.

statement.speaker: fan
statement.text: He scored stage points on lap 100 even though he finished fifth.

options.text: The top ten at each stage end score bonus points (10 down to 1), so he earned those separately from his finish.
Stage points are only for the winner.
Scoring stage points means he finished the stage first.

payload.translation: Stage points go to the top ten at each stage end; they are separate from finish points.

followUps.line: Top ten at the stage end score 10, 9, 8...down to 1 points. A mid-field car can rack up stage points.
followUps.why: This is how fans understand multi-layered scoring.

followUps.line: A driver can finish fifth but score stage points for being top ten at the stage end.
followUps.why: Stage points and finish points compound, which is why stage strategy matters.

lessons.title: Weak spot review
lessons.objective: Review concepts where mastery is below 0.6.

payload.prompt: A 20-gallon fuel cell at a 1.5-mile track burns laps at what pace?

options.text: About 3-4 miles per gallon, so roughly 60-80 laps per tank.
Exactly 100 laps no matter the track or driving.
Only 30 laps because the track is short.

explanation.correct: Close. Fuel mileage varies by track, aero, and driving style, but 60-80 laps per tank is a typical window teams calculate.
explanation.incorrect: Fuel window is not fixed; it depends on track type, aero, and how hard the driver pushes. A 20-gallon tank at a mid-size track typically lasts 60-90 laps.

payload.prompt: After two laps the car is tight in turn 3. On the next stop, which adjustment helps?

facts.label: Problem
facts.value: Front end will not turn; pushing up the track

options.label: Raise tire pressure to loosen the front.
options.consequence: Higher pressure reduces contact patch, freeing up the front to turn.
considerations: Tire pressure is the fastest fix.

options.label: Add wedge to free the front.
options.consequence: Wedge is a cross-weight fix that works, but takes longer to feel.
considerations: Takes a few laps to settle.
Good if pressure does not work.

payload.expertNote: Tight front end (push) in early run means raise tire pressure or reduce wedge weight on that corner.

payload.prompt: At Daytona and Talladega, does the draft bunch the field so tightly that the Big One is likely?

scene.alt: A pack of 20+ cars nose-to-tail at a superspeedway.

choices.label: No, the Big One is just bad luck.

explanation.correct: Right. Pack racing at superspeedways is structural because the draft bunches cars so tightly. One mistake spreads.
explanation.incorrect: At superspeedways, the draft creates pack racing where 30+ cars run nose-to-tail. That tight bunching makes the Big One a predictable risk, not a fluke.

payload.prompt: An {{strategy}} pits early so fresh tires gain time before rivals stop.
payload.template: An {{strategy}} pits early so fresh tires gain time before rivals stop.

explanation.correct: Perfect. The undercut is the classic pit strategy: stop first to get fresh tires before rivals pit.
explanation.incorrect: Undercut means pitting early to get fresh tires and gain time before the field stops. Overcut is the opposite: stay out and let them pit first.

payload.prompt: Match each track type to its defining characteristic.

pairs.definition: Under a mile, tight, bumper-to-bumper; Martinsville is the paperclip.
1-2 miles, all about handling and aero at mid speeds.
2.5+ miles, pack racing, drafting, and the Big One.
Left and right turns, braking zones, ringer drivers shine.

distractorDefinitions: Oval with no banking and one groove.
The fastest track where all engines are 750 hp.

explanation.summary: Track types define the skill sets needed: tight cars at short tracks, balanced handling at intermediates, pack strategy at superspeedways, braking at road courses.

lessons.title: Season refresh
lessons.objective: Refresh rules changes and the current season picture.

payload.prompt: What is the biggest format change in 2026 versus 2014-2025?

options.text: The Chase returned with no eliminations; the top 16 race ten times and most points wins.
Wins now guarantee a playoff spot.

explanation.correct: Exactly. 2026 threw out eliminations and went back to a no-cutoff Chase format where consistency matters more.
explanation.incorrect: In 2026, NASCAR ditched the elimination system (2014-2025) and brought back the Chase with no eliminations. Top 16 in points race ten times; most points at Homestead wins the title.

statement.speaker: fan
statement.text: He won the race and got 55 points, so he is now in contention.

options.text: A win is worth 55 points (up from 40 before 2024), which is a big swing in the regular season.
55 points is a penalty for winning too much.

payload.translation: Since 2024, a win is worth 55 points, which is a significant boost in the championship fight.

followUps.line: 55 for first, 35 for second, 34 for third, down to 1 for 40th. A win is worth 20 more than second.
followUps.why: This gap makes winning important in 2026.

followUps.line: That 55 point swing is why winning in the regular season matters for the Chase seed.
followUps.why: The seed determines the points reset going into ten races.

payload.prompt: The 2026 championship race (race 36) is held at {{track}} in {{month}}.
payload.template: The 2026 championship race (race 36) is held at {{track}} in {{month}}.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Homestead-Miami on Nov 8, 2026 decides the title. It moved back from Phoenix (2020-2025).
explanation.incorrect: The 2026 finale returns to Homestead-Miami on November 8. It was at Phoenix 2020-2025, so this is a return to tradition.

payload.prompt: Does horsepower stay constant across all track types in 2026?

scene.alt: Three NASCAR cars at different track types with varying power settings.

explanation.correct: Right. Horsepower changes by track: 510 hp at superspeedways, 670 at intermediates, 750 at short tracks and road courses.
explanation.incorrect: Horsepower is adjusted by track type via the tapered spacer. Superspeedways get 510 hp (less drag), intermediates 670, and short tracks/road courses 750 (more control and braking).

payload.prompt: Why does the car behind go faster when following closely in a draft?

options.text: The lead car cuts the air so the trailer meets less resistance.
The lead car's engine pushes the car behind forward.
It is an optical illusion; neither car goes faster.

explanation.correct: Exactly. The lead car bears the aerodynamic drag; the trailer in the draft meets less air and gains free speed.
explanation.incorrect: Drafting works because the lead car cuts through air resistance, and the trailing car sits in that wake and feels less drag. Both go faster.

payload.prompt: Caution with 25 laps left: pit for fresh tires or stay out for track position?

facts.label: Leader's fuel
facts.value: Enough to finish if he does not pit

facts.label: Your fuel
facts.value: Can go to the end on current strategy

options.label: Stay out to take the lead.
options.consequence: You inherit first place and track position. Old tires fade but you control the restart.
considerations: Tires will fade, but you are ahead.

options.label: Pit for four fresh tires.
options.consequence: Fresh tires let you race hard at the restart, but you lose track position.
considerations: Fresher is faster on the restart.
Pit strategy is a gamble either way.

payload.expertNote: Track position often beats speed at the end of a run. Staying out is the classic call when fuel is manageable.

payload.prompt: Match each flag to what it signals.

pairs.definition: Start or restart of full-speed racing.
Slow down; incident or debris; pit road is open.
Stop the race completely; big crash or weather.
End of race; first across wins.

explanation.summary: Five flags control the race flow: green (go), yellow (slow), red (stop), white (final lap), checkered (finish).

payload.prompt: Does the regular-season champion start the Chase with any points advantage?

scene.alt: Points reset board showing seed 1 at 2,100 points.

choices.label: Yes, seed 1 gets a head start.
No, all Chase drivers reset to zero.

explanation.correct: Right. Seed 1 (regular-season champ) is reset to 2,100; seed 2 to 2,075; seed 3 to 2,065; seed 4 to 2,060; then -5 per seed down to 2,000 for seed 16.
explanation.incorrect: The points reset rewards consistency. The regular-season champion (seed 1) starts at 2,100 points, which is 100 more than the 16th seed at 2,000.
